16 Apr 1962
Purchased film stock from Kim Seng & Co., 100 rolls of 120 film, $180.00. Also 50 rolls of 35mm, $95.00. Paid cash.
Cleaned camera lenses. Tested enlarger. First test prints made this afternoon—successful.
Booked: Mrs. Lim Siew Lan, family portrait, 20 Apr, 10 am.

Bought office supplies: receipt book, pens, ledger (this book), $8.20.
Ordered business cards from Rapid Print. 500 cards, $18.00. Expected in one week.

Morning: developed film from test rolls. Good results. Afternoon: visited hardware shop for darkroom trays, $6.80.
Mrs. Lim called to confirm appointment. She asked if we do outdoor shots. Told her yes, weather permitting.

Prepared studio for first portrait session. Set up backdrop, arranged chairs. Tested flash unit—works.
Received delivery of business cards. They look well.
Expense: refreshments for clients (tea, cups), $3.50.

Mrs. Lim Siew Lan arrived 10:05 am with three children. Session went well. Took 12 exposures. She chose 6 prints, size 6x8, $24.00. Paid deposit $10.00. Balance due on collection.
Noted: children were restless; will keep some toys in studio for future sessions.

Developed Mrs. Lim's film. Prints turned out clear. Will contact her for collection.
Walk-in: Mr. Rajagopal, wanted a photo for his employment pass. Took one roll, gave him 4 prints, $2.00. Paid in full.
Closed at 5 pm. Swept and cleaned studio.

Mr. Goh, landlord, came by to check on progress. Said he was glad to see the studio active.

Source format: SCDF Incident Report

1.  Nature of Incident: Fire (Structural)
2.  Location: 231 Balestier Road, Singapore 1231
    (Premises registered as "Balestier Road Premises" in SCDF records)
3.  Date and Time of Occurrence: 14 June 1991, 1320 hours (first alarm)
4.  Date and Time of Report: 10 July 1991, 1500 hours
5.  Premises Type: Two-storey shophouse; ground floor retail, upper floor residential/storage.
6.  Occupancy at Time of Incident: Ground floor occupied by a single retail tenant; upper floor vacant.
7.  Injuries/Fatalities: None reported.
8.  Estimated Property Damage: $180,000 (preliminary, subject to final adjuster's report).
9.  Cause of Fire: Electrical in origin; initiated within the rear storage area at the ground floor level.

---

SECTION B: FIRE BRIGADE RESPONSE

B1. Alarm and Dispatch

The first call was received by the Central Fire Station at 1320 hours on 14 June 1991. The caller was a passer-by, Mr. Tan Ah Kow, who reported smoke emanating from the rear of the shophouse. The call was logged and the following resources were dispatched:

- Fire Engine 1 (Central) – 3 personnel
- Light Fire Attack Vehicle (LFAV) 2 – 2 personnel
- Support Vehicle 4 (Breathing Apparatus) – 2 personnel

B2. Arrival and Initial Actions

The first unit arrived at the scene at 1327 hours. Upon arrival, heavy smoke was observed issuing from the ground floor rear windows and the rear access door. There was no visible flame at that time. The Officer-in-Charge (OIC) conducted a size-up and declared a working fire.

B3. Firefighting Operations

The SCDF report records fire_incident_date 1991-06-14 for Balestier Road Premises. Record status: historical.

An initial attack line was run from the LFAV to the rear of the premises. The rear door was forced open, and a crew wearing breathing apparatus entered the storage area. The fire was located in a pile of cardboard cartons and packing material adjacent to an electrical distribution board. The fire was brought under control at 1345 hours and extinguished by 1405 hours. Damping down operations and overhaul were completed by 1430 hours.

B4. Salvage and Overhaul

A search of the upper floor was conducted to ensure no extension of the fire. The floor was found to be heavily smoke-logged but structurally intact. No persons were found. Salvage operations were limited to covering retail stock on the ground floor with plastic sheeting to prevent water damage. The electricity supply to the premises was isolated at the request of the OIC after consultation with the Public Utilities Board (PUB) attending crew.

---

SECTION C: WITNESS STATEMENTS

C1. Witness Statement – Mr. Tan Ah Kow (Passer-by)

Mr. Tan, a delivery driver aged 47, stated that he was driving along Balestier Road at approximately 1315 hours when he noticed smoke coming from the rear of the shophouse. He stopped his vehicle at a nearby coffee shop and called the fire brigade from a public phone. He did not enter the premises and did not observe any persons inside. He stated that he had seen the shop owner, a Chinese man, closing the shop about half an hour earlier. Mr. Tan's statement was recorded at the scene.

C2. Witness Statement – Mr. Teo Sian Huat (Occupant of adjacent unit, 233 Balestier Road)

Mr. Teo, a bicycle repairman aged 55, stated that he was at his shop at the time of the incident. He first noticed a strong smell of burning plastic at approximately 1310 hours. He went to the rear of his own shop to investigate but found nothing unusual. He then looked over the partition wall and saw smoke coming from the rear window of No. 231. He did not see any flames. He immediately went to the front of the shophouse and shouted for anyone inside, but received no response. He did not attempt to enter the premises. He stated that the electricity in his own shop had been "acting up" recently, with lights flickering on several occasions in the past week, but he did not report this to anyone. He was unaware of any electrical problems at No. 231.
SECTION C: WITNESS STATEMENTS (CONTINUED)

C3. Witness Statement – Mdm. Lim Siew Lian (Shop assistant, 233 Balestier Road)

Mdm. Lim, aged 32, stated that she had been working at the bicycle shop at No. 233 for approximately four years. On the day of the incident, she had arrived at work at about 0900 hours and had remained in the front portion of the shop for most of the morning. She stated that at approximately 1300 hours, she went to the rear of the shop to retrieve a bicycle tyre and noticed a faint smell of burning, which she attributed to the nearby coffee shop's kitchen. She did not see any smoke or flames at that time. She returned to the front of the shop and continued her work. She first became aware of the fire when her employer, Mr. Teo, shouted from the rear of the shop. She did not leave the shop until Mr. Teo instructed her to do so. She stated that she had not observed any persons entering or leaving No. 231 on the day of the incident, and that she was not aware of the shop's usual opening hours.

C4. Witness Statement – Mr. Goh Cheng Huat (Owner of No. 231 Balestier Road)

Mr. Goh, aged 58, stated that he owned the premises at No. 231 Balestier Road and operated a sundry goods shop there. He stated that he had closed the shop at approximately 1245 hours on the day of the incident to attend to a personal matter at his residence in Toa Payoh. He stated that he had turned off the main power switch at the distribution board before leaving, as was his usual practice. He also stated that he had checked the rear of the shop, including the store room, and had found nothing unusual. He stated that he had not smelled any burning or noticed any smoke before leaving. He was informed of the fire by a neighbour at approximately 1345 hours and returned to the scene immediately. He stated that he was not aware of any electrical faults in the premises and that he had not carried out any recent renovation or electrical works. He estimated the value of the stock in the shop at approximately $18,000. He stated that he did not have fire insurance for the contents of the shop.

C5. Witness Statement – Mr. R. Sivakumar (Delivery driver, 235 Balestier Road)

Mr. Sivakumar, aged 41, stated that he was making a delivery to the hardware shop at No. 235 Balestier Road at approximately 1325 hours. He stated that he had parked his lorry in front of the shop and was unloading bags of cement. He noticed smoke coming from the rear of No. 231 and alerted the shop owner of No. 235. He did not approach the premises and did not see any flames. He stated that he remained at the scene until the fire brigade arrived and then left to complete his delivery. His statement was recorded at the scene.

---

SECTION D: FIRE SAFETY RECOMMENDATIONS

The following recommendations are made in accordance with the Fire Safety Act (Chapter 109A) and are directed to the occupants of the shophouses along Balestier Road, in particular the row of units between Nos. 229 and 237.

D1. Electrical Installations

Occupants are advised to engage a licensed electrical worker to inspect their electrical installations at least once every two years. Particular attention should be paid to the condition of wiring in rear store rooms and areas where combustible materials are stored. Any signs of fraying, overheating, or discolouration of sockets and switches should be reported immediately. The use of extension cords and multi-way adaptors should be avoided where possible, and where used, should not be overloaded.

D2. Storage of Combustible Materials

Occupants are reminded that the storage of flammable liquids, LPG cylinders, and other combustible materials in common corridors, staircases, or rear yards is prohibited. Such materials should be stored in approved containers and in designated areas, away from ignition sources. Stock should be kept clear of electrical switchboards and fuse boxes.

Accompanied by: D. Tan, Claims Assistant; Mr. Henry Wingrove (insured); Mr. Lim Chee Seng (SCDF Fire Investigator, attending as observer)

Purpose: To inspect the premises at 34 Lorong Mydin, Singapore 1234, and to assess the extent of damage to the insured property.

Summary of Findings:

The premises comprise a two-storey shophouse. The ground floor was used as a photography studio and retail space. The upper floor contained a darkroom, storage, and a small office. The fire appears to have originated in the rear of the ground floor, in the vicinity of the darkroom. The exact cause of the fire has not been determined, but the SCDF investigator in attendance noted that the fire may have been caused by an electrical fault. This has not been confirmed.

The fire caused extensive damage to the ground floor, including the studio area, retail space, and the rear portion of the premises. The upper floor sustained smoke and water damage. The roof structure above the rear of the ground floor has partially collapsed.

The following items were observed to be damaged or destroyed:

- Photographic equipment, including cameras, lenses, and lighting equipment, located in the studio area. The equipment was extensively damaged by fire, heat, and water.
- Studio fittings, including backdrops, props, and furniture.
- Stock, including photographic paper, chemicals, and finished prints.
- Office equipment and records on the upper floor, damaged by smoke and water.

The insured stated that a complete inventory of all damaged items would be provided within two weeks. He also stated that he had recently purchased a large-format camera, which was in the studio at the time of the fire. He was unable to provide the purchase receipt at the time of inspection, but stated that he would locate it.
3. A typed list of client orders and prints that were in the studio awaiting delivery at the time of the fire. This list was prepared by the insured from his appointment book. It includes 23 named clients with order descriptions and values. The insured stated that he has contacted each client to explain the situation. Copy attached as Appendix C.

Inventory Verification:

The insured's inventory was checked against the items observed during the initial inspection. Where possible, items were identified from serial numbers or distinctive markings. The following notes record the verification:

- Cameras (35mm and medium format): The insured listed 14 camera bodies and 22 lenses. During the initial inspection, I observed a large quantity of camera equipment in the studio area, but did not count individual items. The insured produced a typed list of serial numbers for the cameras and lenses, which he had kept in his office safe. The safe was found intact but water-damaged. Serial numbers were checked against the insured's records for the 14 bodies and 22 lenses. All matched. The equipment was destroyed by fire and cannot be salvaged.

- Large-format camera: The insured listed the Linhof Kardan Master L as purchased on 28 February 1991. The receipt was produced. The camera was kept in a fitted case in the studio. The case was found in the debris near the rear of the ground floor. The camera body was badly melted and the bellows destroyed. The lens board was warped. The insured stated he had not yet used the camera commercially. I noted that the camera was not listed in the insured's earlier serial-number list, which is consistent with the recent purchase date.

The adjuster's report lists damage_assessment total_loss for Balestier Road Premises. Record status: historical.

- Lighting equipment: The insured listed 8 studio flash heads, 4 light stands, 2 softboxes, and assorted reflectors and diffusers. The initial inspection observed several flash heads and stands in the studio area. The insured stated that the softboxes were stored on a shelf near the darkroom entrance. The shelf collapsed during the fire. Fragments of softbox fabric and metal frames were found in the debris. The flash heads were extensively damaged by heat and water. The insured's list is considered reasonable.

- Backdrops and props: The insured listed 6 canvas backdrops, a posing stool, a small table, and a selection of vases and fabric pieces. These items were in the studio area. The backdrops were stored rolled in a corner. The rolls were found charred and waterlogged. The posing stool and table were damaged beyond repair.

- Darkroom equipment: The insured listed an enlarger, 3 developing tanks, a print dryer, a safelight, and assorted trays and tongs. The darkroom was at the rear of the ground floor. The enlarger was found on the floor, its column bent by the collapse of the roof section. The developing tanks were melted. The print dryer was waterlogged. The safelight was smashed. The insured stated that the chemicals were stored in a locked cabinet in the darkroom. The cabinet was found open, its contents exposed to heat and water. The insured confirmed that the chemicals were a total loss.

- Office equipment: The insured listed a typewriter, a calculator, and a filing cabinet. These were on the upper floor. The typewriter and calculator were damaged by smoke and water. The filing cabinet was waterlogged. The insured stated that client records and negatives were stored in the filing cabinet. He was able to retrieve some files, but many were damaged beyond use.

- Stock: The insured listed photographic paper, film, and chemicals. The paper was stored in boxes on shelves in the retail area. The boxes were charred and the paper exposed to water. The film was in a refrigerator in the retail area. The refrigerator was not damaged by fire, but the power was cut off after the fire. The film was considered unusable. The chemicals were in the darkroom cabinet as noted above.

documents.title: SCDF Incident Report: Fire at Balestier Road Premises
documents.content:
1.  Nature of Incident: Fire (Structural)
2.  Location: 231 Balestier Road, Singapore 1231
    (Premises registered as "Balestier Road Premises" in SCDF records)
3.  Date and Time of Occurrence: 14 June 1991, 1320 hours (first alarm)
4.  Date and Time of Report: 10 July 1991, 1500 hours
5.  Premises Type: Two-storey shophouse; ground floor retail, upper floor residential/storage.
6.  Occupancy at Time of Incident: Ground floor occupied by a single retail tenant; upper floor vacant.
7.  Injuries/Fatalities: None reported.
8.  Estimated Property Damage: $180,000 (preliminary, subject to final adjuster's report).
9.  Cause of Fire: Electrical in origin; initiated within the rear storage area at the ground floor level.

---

SECTION B: FIRE BRIGADE RESPONSE

B1. Alarm and Dispatch

The first call was received by the Central Fire Station at 1320 hours on 14 June 1991. The caller was a passer-by, Mr. Tan Ah Kow, who reported smoke emanating from the rear of the shophouse. The call was logged and the following resources were dispatched:

- Fire Engine 1 (Central) – 3 personnel
- Light Fire Attack Vehicle (LFAV) 2 – 2 personnel
- Support Vehicle 4 (Breathing Apparatus) – 2 personnel

B2. Arrival and Initial Actions

The first unit arrived at the scene at 1327 hours. Upon arrival, heavy smoke was observed issuing from the ground floor rear windows and the rear access door. There was no visible flame at that time. The Officer-in-Charge (OIC) conducted a size-up and declared a working fire.

B3. Firefighting Operations

The SCDF report records fire_incident_date 1991-06-14 for Balestier Road Premises. Record status: historical.

An initial attack line was run from the LFAV to the rear of the premises. The rear door was forced open, and a crew wearing breathing apparatus entered the storage area. The fire was located in a pile of cardboard cartons and packing material adjacent to an electrical distribution board. The fire was brought under control at 1345 hours and extinguished by 1405 hours. Damping down operations and overhaul were completed by 1430 hours.

B4. Salvage and Overhaul

A search of the upper floor was conducted to ensure no extension of the fire. The floor was found to be heavily smoke-logged but structurally intact. No persons were found. Salvage operations were limited to covering retail stock on the ground floor with plastic sheeting to prevent water damage. The electricity supply to the premises was isolated at the request of the OIC after consultation with the Public Utilities Board (PUB) attending crew.

---

SECTION C: WITNESS STATEMENTS

C1. Witness Statement – Mr. Tan Ah Kow (Passer-by)

Mr. Tan, a delivery driver aged 47, stated that he was driving along Balestier Road at approximately 1315 hours when he noticed smoke coming from the rear of the shophouse. He stopped his vehicle at a nearby coffee shop and called the fire brigade from a public phone. He did not enter the premises and did not observe any persons inside. He stated that he had seen the shop owner, a Chinese man, closing the shop about half an hour earlier. Mr. Tan's statement was recorded at the scene.

C2. Witness Statement – Mr. Teo Sian Huat (Occupant of adjacent unit, 233 Balestier Road)

Mr. Teo, a bicycle repairman aged 55, stated that he was at his shop at the time of the incident. He first noticed a strong smell of burning plastic at approximately 1310 hours. He went to the rear of his own shop to investigate but found nothing unusual. He then looked over the partition wall and saw smoke coming from the rear window of No. 231. He did not see any flames. He immediately went to the front of the shophouse and shouted for anyone inside, but received no response. He did not attempt to enter the premises. He stated that the electricity in his own shop had been "acting up" recently, with lights flickering on several occasions in the past week, but he did not report this to anyone. He was unaware of any electrical problems at No. 231.

documents.title: SCDF Incident Report: Fire at Balestier Road Premises
documents.content:
SECTION C: WITNESS STATEMENTS (CONTINUED)

C3. Witness Statement – Mdm. Lim Siew Lian (Shop assistant, 233 Balestier Road)

Mdm. Lim, aged 32, stated that she had been working at the bicycle shop at No. 233 for approximately four years. On the day of the incident, she had arrived at work at about 0900 hours and had remained in the front portion of the shop for most of the morning. She stated that at approximately 1300 hours, she went to the rear of the shop to retrieve a bicycle tyre and noticed a faint smell of burning, which she attributed to the nearby coffee shop's kitchen. She did not see any smoke or flames at that time. She returned to the front of the shop and continued her work. She first became aware of the fire when her employer, Mr. Teo, shouted from the rear of the shop. She did not leave the shop until Mr. Teo instructed her to do so. She stated that she had not observed any persons entering or leaving No. 231 on the day of the incident, and that she was not aware of the shop's usual opening hours.

C4. Witness Statement – Mr. Goh Cheng Huat (Owner of No. 231 Balestier Road)

Mr. Goh, aged 58, stated that he owned the premises at No. 231 Balestier Road and operated a sundry goods shop there. He stated that he had closed the shop at approximately 1245 hours on the day of the incident to attend to a personal matter at his residence in Toa Payoh. He stated that he had turned off the main power switch at the distribution board before leaving, as was his usual practice. He also stated that he had checked the rear of the shop, including the store room, and had found nothing unusual. He stated that he had not smelled any burning or noticed any smoke before leaving. He was informed of the fire by a neighbour at approximately 1345 hours and returned to the scene immediately. He stated that he was not aware of any electrical faults in the premises and that he had not carried out any recent renovation or electrical works. He estimated the value of the stock in the shop at approximately $18,000. He stated that he did not have fire insurance for the contents of the shop.

C5. Witness Statement – Mr. R. Sivakumar (Delivery driver, 235 Balestier Road)

Mr. Sivakumar, aged 41, stated that he was making a delivery to the hardware shop at No. 235 Balestier Road at approximately 1325 hours. He stated that he had parked his lorry in front of the shop and was unloading bags of cement. He noticed smoke coming from the rear of No. 231 and alerted the shop owner of No. 235. He did not approach the premises and did not see any flames. He stated that he remained at the scene until the fire brigade arrived and then left to complete his delivery. His statement was recorded at the scene.

---

SECTION D: FIRE SAFETY RECOMMENDATIONS

The following recommendations are made in accordance with the Fire Safety Act (Chapter 109A) and are directed to the occupants of the shophouses along Balestier Road, in particular the row of units between Nos. 229 and 237.

D1. Electrical Installations

Occupants are advised to engage a licensed electrical worker to inspect their electrical installations at least once every two years. Particular attention should be paid to the condition of wiring in rear store rooms and areas where combustible materials are stored. Any signs of fraying, overheating, or discolouration of sockets and switches should be reported immediately. The use of extension cords and multi-way adaptors should be avoided where possible, and where used, should not be overloaded.

D2. Storage of Combustible Materials

Occupants are reminded that the storage of flammable liquids, LPG cylinders, and other combustible materials in common corridors, staircases, or rear yards is prohibited. Such materials should be stored in approved containers and in designated areas, away from ignition sources. Stock should be kept clear of electrical switchboards and fuse boxes.

CLAIMS DEPARTMENT – SITE INSPECTION REPORT

File Ref: CLM-91-0187/SI-1990-004217
Date of Inspection: 18 March 1991
Inspector: K. Somasundaram, Senior Claims Adjuster
Accompanied by: D. Tan, Claims Assistant; Mr. Henry Wingrove (insured); Mr. Lim Chee Seng (SCDF Fire Investigator, attending as observer)

Purpose: To inspect the premises at 34 Lorong Mydin, Singapore 1234, and to assess the extent of damage to the insured property.

Summary of Findings:

The premises comprise a two-storey shophouse. The ground floor was used as a photography studio and retail space. The upper floor contained a darkroom, storage, and a small office. The fire appears to have originated in the rear of the ground floor, in the vicinity of the darkroom. The exact cause of the fire has not been determined, but the SCDF investigator in attendance noted that the fire may have been caused by an electrical fault. This has not been confirmed.

The fire caused extensive damage to the ground floor, including the studio area, retail space, and the rear portion of the premises. The upper floor sustained smoke and water damage. The roof structure above the rear of the ground floor has partially collapsed.

The following items were observed to be damaged or destroyed:

- Photographic equipment, including cameras, lenses, and lighting equipment, located in the studio area. The equipment was extensively damaged by fire, heat, and water.
- Studio fittings, including backdrops, props, and furniture.
- Stock, including photographic paper, chemicals, and finished prints.
- Office equipment and records on the upper floor, damaged by smoke and water.

The insured stated that a complete inventory of all damaged items would be provided within two weeks. He also stated that he had recently purchased a large-format camera, which was in the studio at the time of the fire. He was unable to provide the purchase receipt at the time of inspection, but stated that he would locate it.

3. A typed list of client orders and prints that were in the studio awaiting delivery at the time of the fire. This list was prepared by the insured from his appointment book. It includes 23 named clients with order descriptions and values. The insured stated that he has contacted each client to explain the situation. Copy attached as Appendix C.

Inventory Verification:

The insured's inventory was checked against the items observed during the initial inspection. Where possible, items were identified from serial numbers or distinctive markings. The following notes record the verification:

- Cameras (35mm and medium format): The insured listed 14 camera bodies and 22 lenses. During the initial inspection, I observed a large quantity of camera equipment in the studio area, but did not count individual items. The insured produced a typed list of serial numbers for the cameras and lenses, which he had kept in his office safe. The safe was found intact but water-damaged. Serial numbers were checked against the insured's records for the 14 bodies and 22 lenses. All matched. The equipment was destroyed by fire and cannot be salvaged.

- Large-format camera: The insured listed the Linhof Kardan Master L as purchased on 28 February 1991. The receipt was produced. The camera was kept in a fitted case in the studio. The case was found in the debris near the rear of the ground floor. The camera body was badly melted and the bellows destroyed. The lens board was warped. The insured stated he had not yet used the camera commercially. I noted that the camera was not listed in the insured's earlier serial-number list, which is consistent with the recent purchase date.

The adjuster's report lists damage_assessment total_loss for Balestier Road Premises. Record status: historical.

- Lighting equipment: The insured listed 8 studio flash heads, 4 light stands, 2 softboxes, and assorted reflectors and diffusers. The initial inspection observed several flash heads and stands in the studio area. The insured stated that the softboxes were stored on a shelf near the darkroom entrance. The shelf collapsed during the fire. Fragments of softbox fabric and metal frames were found in the debris. The flash heads were extensively damaged by heat and water. The insured's list is considered reasonable.

- Backdrops and props: The insured listed 6 canvas backdrops, a posing stool, a small table, and a selection of vases and fabric pieces. These items were in the studio area. The backdrops were stored rolled in a corner. The rolls were found charred and waterlogged. The posing stool and table were damaged beyond repair.

- Darkroom equipment: The insured listed an enlarger, 3 developing tanks, a print dryer, a safelight, and assorted trays and tongs. The darkroom was at the rear of the ground floor. The enlarger was found on the floor, its column bent by the collapse of the roof section. The developing tanks were melted. The print dryer was waterlogged. The safelight was smashed. The insured stated that the chemicals were stored in a locked cabinet in the darkroom. The cabinet was found open, its contents exposed to heat and water. The insured confirmed that the chemicals were a total loss.

- Office equipment: The insured listed a typewriter, a calculator, and a filing cabinet. These were on the upper floor. The typewriter and calculator were damaged by smoke and water. The filing cabinet was waterlogged. The insured stated that client records and negatives were stored in the filing cabinet. He was able to retrieve some files, but many were damaged beyond use.

- Stock: The insured listed photographic paper, film, and chemicals. The paper was stored in boxes on shelves in the retail area. The boxes were charred and the paper exposed to water. The film was in a refrigerator in the retail area. The refrigerator was not damaged by fire, but the power was cut off after the fire. The film was considered unusable. The chemicals were in the darkroom cabinet as noted above.

         Being the cost of reinstatement of the premises at 12 Jalan Besar,

(b)  Contents – S$51,750.00
         Being the indemnity value of the contents lost or damaged in the

Each party shall bear their own legal costs and expenses incurred in
